IX.}}</noinclude>prohibited him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=39}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} said, Do not prohibit him. for there is no man that doth a miracle in my name, and can soone speake il of me. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=40}}† for he that is not against you, is for you. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=41}}† For vvhosoeuer shal giue you to drinke a cuppe of vvater in my name, because you are Christs: amen I say to you, he shal not lose his {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Reward for almes deedes, whereby it is euident they be meritorious.}}∷ revvard. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=42}}† And vvhosoeuer shal {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ To giue scandal by our life to the weake in faith, is a great sinne, specially in Priests, Preachers, and Princes.}}∷ scandalize one of these litle ones beleeuing in me: it is good for him rather if a milstone vvere put about his necke, and he vvere cast into the sea. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=43}}† And if thy hand scandalize thee, cut it of. it is good for thee to enter into life, maimed, then hauing tvvo hands to goe into hel, into the fire vnquencheable, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=44}}† vvhere their vvorme dieth not, and the fire quencheth not. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=45}}† And if thy foote scandalize thee, choppe it of. it is good for thee to enter into life euerlasting, lame, rather then hauing tvvo feete, to be cast into the hel of vnquencheable fire, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=46}}† vvhere their vvorme dieth not, and the fire quencheth not. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=47}}† And if thine eye scandalize thee, cast it out. it is good for thee vvith one eye to enter into the kingdom of God, rather then hauing tvvo eies, to be cast into the hel of fire, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=48}}† vvhere their vvorme dieth not, and the fire quencheth not. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=49}}† For euery one shal be salted vvith fire: and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 2, 13.''}}* euery victime shal be salted vvith salt. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=50}}† Salt is good. but if the salt shal be vnseasoned: vvhervvith vvil you season it? Haue salt in you, and haue peace among you.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. IX.}}}}

''4. Elias with Moyses.'') {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Elias. Moyses.}}Moyses representeth the persons of al the Saincts that shal be departed this life when Christ commeth in his Maiestie to iudgement: And Elias (who was then liuing) figureth the holy men that shal then be found aliue when he commeth in glorie. Who both shal then begin to reigne with Christ in glorie. ''Beda in 9. Marc.''

''13. Elias also is come.'') Elias was Zelous for Gods Law, a great reprehender of sinne, and an Eremite{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Elias and Iohn Baptist Eremites.}}, and shal be the Precursor of Christ in his second Aduent: So was Iohn before his first Aduent, a Zelatour, a Corrector, an Eremite, and his Precursor. ''Theod. in caten. Thomæ super hunc locum''. See S. Hierom in the life of Paul the eremite, that both Elias and Iohn Baptist vvere counted principal professours of that life.

''38. In thy name.'') {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The name of {{sc|Iesvs}} worketh miracles.}}Miracles are vvrought sometime by the name of {{sc|Iesvs}}, whatsoeuer the men be, when it is for the proofe of a truth or for the glorie of God. In so much that Iulian the Apostata him selfe did driue away diuels with the signe of the Crosse: as ''S. Gregorie Nazianzene'' writeth ''orat. 1 in Iulian. Theodoret. li. 3 c. 3 hist''. And so also Heretikes may doe miracles among the Heathen, to prooue any article of the Christian faith: but they neuer did nor euer shal vvorke any miracle to prooue any of their erroneous opinions, as to prooue that Christ is not really in the B. Sacrament.<noinclude>{{rh|||Chap. X.}}</noinclude>
